353172.title: Cone conjecture for characteristic-dependent Betti numbers of graph ideals
353172.statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices, and let $I(G)\subseteq k[x_1,\dots,x_n]$ be its edge ideal. Introduce a new vertex $n+1$ and set

$$
J=I(G)+x_{n+1}(x_1,\dots,x_n)\subseteq k[x_1,\dots,x_n,x_{n+1}],
$$

which is the edge ideal of the cone over $G$. Betti numbers are computed over the coefficient field $k$.

**Cone conjecture.** If the Betti numbers of $I(G)$ depend on the field, then the Betti numbers of $J^2$ also depend on the field.

The conjecture is motivated by numerous computer experiments and asks whether adjoining a cone vertex preserves characteristic dependence at the level of the square. Its general validity is not established in the source.

353177.title: Baril–Kirgizov–Vajnovszki conjecture on 1-Gray codes for restricted binary words
353177.statement: Let $\mathcal{W}_{q,n}$ denote the set of restricted binary words of length $n$ associated with the positive rational parameter $q$. A **1-Gray code** is an arrangement of all words in which consecutive words differ in at most one position. **Baril–Kirgizov–Vajnovszki conjecture.** For given $q \in \mathbb{N}^+$ and $n \ge 0$, a 1-Gray code exists for $\mathcal{W}_{q,n}$. This extends the known existence of a 3-Gray code and is motivated by the Eğecioğlu–Iršič conjecture, proved for $q=1$; the assertion is based on experimental evidence for small values of $n$ and $q$ and remains open in the supplied source.

353203.title: Uniqueness conjecture for power domination reconfiguration graphs of complete bipartite graphs
353203.statement: Let $K_{s,t}$ be the complete bipartite graph with part sizes $s$ and $t$, and let $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ denote its power domination reconfiguration graph under token addition/removal reconfiguration. **Uniqueness conjecture.** $\mathscr{PD}^{TAR}(K_{s,t})$ is unique if and only if $s\ne 2$ and $t\ne 2$. This is supported by the uniqueness results for $K_{1,t}$ with $t\ge 3$ and $K_{3,3}$, together with Sage computations for $s\in\{3,4\}$ and $t\in\{3,4,5\}$; the conjecture proposes the complete characterization, including the cases not covered by those results.

353321.title: The characterization of good ordered graphs by monotone caterpillars
353321.statement:
Let $G^<$ be a connected ordered graph. An ordered graph is **good** if it has the corresponding ordered Ramsey property used in the paper, and a **monotone caterpillar graph** is the class characterized in the source by the forbidden ordered subgraphs in Figure 2.

**Monotone-caterpillar characterization conjecture.** The ordered graph $G^<$ is good if and only if it is a monotone caterpillar graph.

The authors found no counterexamples among the small graphs they exhaustively searched and verified that there are no $4$-good graphs with at most six vertices other than monotone caterpillar graphs. A proof of the characterization remains open.

353451.title: Stressed-hyperplane relaxation conjecture for Ehrhart positivity
353451.statement:
Let $M$ be an Ehrhart-positive matroid, meaning that the coefficients of its Ehrhart polynomial are nonnegative, and let $H$ be a **stressed hyperplane** in $M$. Write $\operatorname{Rel}_H(M)$ for the matroid obtained by relaxing $H$.

**Stressed-hyperplane relaxation conjecture.** If $M$ is Ehrhart positive and $H$ is a stressed hyperplane in $M$, then $\operatorname{Rel}_H(M)$ is also Ehrhart positive.

This is presented alongside the panhandle positivity conjecture and is supported by substantial computational evidence. Its resolution status is not specified in the supplied text.

359900.title: Completeness conjecture for equality cases of Stanley's inequalities
359900.statement: Let $\operatorname{EqualityStanley}_k$ denote the relevant equality-verification problem for the $k$th Stanley inequality. **EqualityStanley completeness conjecture.** The problem $\operatorname{EqualityStanley}_k$ is $\mathrm{C_=P}$-complete for sufficiently large $k$. The source presents this as an assertion in a conjecture environment but supplies no resolution or further explanation of the encoding; it concerns the computational complexity of equality cases for Stanley-type matroid inequalities.

360113.title: Polynomial-time indistinguishability conjecture for planted and unplanted number partitioning
360113.statement:
Let p-\texttt{NPP} and u-\texttt{NPP} denote the planted and unplanted random number partitioning problems, respectively. For a fixed $c>1$, consider distinguishing these two models in the regime described by the hypothesis-testing problem.

**Polynomial-time indistinguishability conjecture.** Fix any $c>1$. There exists no polynomial-time algorithm that distinguishes the p-\texttt{NPP} from the u-\texttt{NPP} with probability greater than $\frac12$.

This conjecture concerns the computational tractability of hypothesis testing between the planted and unplanted models. The source motivates it by noting statistical distinguishability when values below $2^{-cn}$ occur, while leaving efficient distinguishing open.

360324.title: Existence of limiting proportions of zero types in symmetric-group character tables
360324.statement:
For each $n$, let $S_n$ be the symmetric group, and let $z_I(S_n)$, $z_{I\!I}(S_n)$, and $z(S_n)$ denote respectively the proportions of character-table zeros of type I, of type II, and of all zeros in the character table of $S_n$. **Existence conjecture.** The limits

$$
\lim_{n\to\infty}z_I(S_n),\qquad \lim_{n\to\infty}z_{I\!I}(S_n),\qquad \lim_{n\to\infty}z(S_n)
$$

exist. Numerical experiments suggest convergence, but the paper does not establish these limits.

360345.title: Bounded-excess connectivity conjecture for Tverberg partition graphs
360345.statement:
Let $S$ be a finite set of points in $\mathds{R}^d$, let $r$ be a positive integer, and let $G_T[S,r]$ denote the Tverberg $r$-partition graph of $S$. Let

$$
\operatorname{Tv}(d,r)=(d+1)(r-1)+1.
$$

**The bounded-excess connectivity conjecture.** There exists a constant $k(d)$ depending only on $d$ such that $G_T[S,r]$ is connected whenever

$$
|S|\geq \operatorname{Tv}(d,r)+k(d),
$$

with $k(1)=1$. The authors motivate this by the general connectivity bound and computational observations in the plane, and conjecture that the bound $3\operatorname{Tv}(d,r)-1$ is not optimal; the source does not resolve the existence of such a dimension-dependent constant.

360565.title: PSPACE-completeness conjecture for the B- and B'-games
360565.statement: The Builder-Blocker general position games are played on a graph, with Builder and Blocker alternately selecting vertices according to the rules defining the games; the associated decision problems ask whether Builder has a winning strategy. **PSPACE-completeness conjecture.** The decision version of the B- and B'-games are PSPACE-complete. This conjecture concerns the computational complexity of deciding the winner in these games and is motivated by the known hardness of the avoidment game; its resolution is left as an open problem.

360575.title: Indecomposability conjecture for disconnected regular Schur labeled skew shape modules
360575.statement:
Let $P\in\sfRSP_n$ be a regular Schur labeled skew shape poset, and let $\sh(\tau_P)$ denote its associated skew shape. A disconnected ribbon is a ribbon contained in a disconnected skew shape in the sense used in the paper.

**Indecomposability conjecture.** If $\sh(\tau_P)$ is disconnected and contains no disconnected ribbon, then the associated module $\sfM_P$ is indecomposable.

The converse to the paper's obstruction result is known when $\sh(\tau_P)$ is connected and was verified computationally for $|P|\leq 6$ in the disconnected case. The conjecture asserts the general disconnected case.

360623.title: Non-membership conjecture for the sign-imbalance problem in #P
360623.statement:
For a poset $P$, its sign imbalance is the absolute difference between the numbers of even and odd linear extensions. The computational problem **Sign Imbalance** takes a poset $P$ as input and outputs its sign imbalance; the class $\mathsf{\#P}$ consists of functions counting accepting paths of nondeterministic polynomial-time computations. **Sign Imbalance non-membership conjecture.**

$$
\textsc{Sign Imbalance}\notin\mathsf{\#P}.
$$

Sign imbalance is naturally in the counting-difference class $\mathsf{GapP}$, but the source states that its non-membership in $\mathsf{\#P}$ remains open.

360681.title: Conjecture that minimal-base cardinalities form an interval for primitive groups
360681.statement:
Let $G$ be a primitive permutation group on a domain $\Omega$, and let $\mathcal{M}(G,\Omega)$ denote the set of cardinalities of minimal bases of $G$ on $\Omega$. **Primitive interval conjecture.** The set $\mathcal{M}(G,\Omega)$ is an interval of natural numbers.

The conjecture reflects the absence of known primitive examples for which the set of minimal-base cardinalities is not an interval. It concerns the structure of minimal bases in primitive permutation groups; the source reports only computational evidence and no additional confirmation.

361110.title: Bipartite characterization of rational POP generating functions
361110.statement:
Let a **POP class** be a permutation class defined by avoidance of partially ordered patterns. Its generating function is the ordinary generating function of its counting sequence, and the class is **bipartite** when its defining partially ordered pattern has a bipartite underlying poset.

**Bipartite characterization conjecture.** A POP class has a rational generating function if and only if it is bipartite.

The conjecture strengthens the computational observation that the size-$5$ POP classes found with rational generating functions were bipartite and had regular insertion encodings. The supplied context notes that the available regular-insertion-encoding results do not prove that non-regular classes cannot have rational generating functions.

361189.title: The deficient path forest conjecture on impossibly burnable forests
361189.statement:
For $m\in\mathbb{N}$ and $1\leq l\leq m^2$, let $B_m(l)$ be the least positive integer $t$ having the same parity as $l$ such that

$$
l\leq\sum_{i=1}^t[2m-(2i-1)]=2mt-t^2.
$$

Let $T=(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_n)$ be an $n$-path forest of order $m^2$. Call $T$ **deficient** when it cannot be burned in $m$ rounds, and call it **impossibly burnable** when

$$
\sum_{i=1}^n B_m(l_i)>m.
$$

**Deficient path forest conjecture.** Let $n\geq4$. If $T$ is a deficient $n$-path forest with $l_1\geq L_{n-1}$, then $T$ is impossibly burnable. The conjecture is motivated by computational verification for small values of $n$, but its general validity remains open.

361213.title: Conjecture on odd-characteristic BCH codes with prescribed dual distance and locality
361213.statement: Let $q=p^s$, where $p$ is an odd prime and $s\ge 2$, and set $h=\frac{p-1}{2}$. Let $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,3,h)}$ denote the BCH code in question. **BCH-code conjecture.** The code $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,3,h)}$ is an AMDS code with parameters $[q+1,q-3,4]$, while its dual has parameters $[q+1,4,q-p]$. Moreover, $\mathcal{C}_{(q,q+1,3,h)}$ is a $d$-optimal and $k$-optimal LRC with locality $q-p-1$, and its dual is an LRC with locality $3$. The claim is motivated by computations for even $s$ and several values of $p$; the preceding theorem establishes related parameter and locality results, but the asserted exact dual distance and locality remain unproved in the stated generality.

361744.title: Häggkvist's Hamiltonicity conjecture for oriented graphs
361744.statement:
Let $D$ be an oriented graph on $n$ vertices. Define

$$
\delta^*(D)=\delta(D)+\delta^+(D)+\delta^-(D).
$$

**Häggkvist's conjecture.** Every oriented graph $D$ with

$$
\delta^*(D)>\frac{3n-3}{2}
$$

is Hamiltonian.

This conjecture was verified approximately by Kelly: the weaker condition $\delta^*(D)\geq (3/2+o(1))n$ guarantees Hamiltonicity. The exact threshold stated here is therefore resolved according to the supplied status evidence.

382188.title: The good GKP codes conjecture for random NTRU lattices
382188.statement:
Let $L$ be the NTRU lattice specified by the basis in equation (HCS), and let

$$
R_q=\mathbb{Z}_q[x]/\langle x^n-1\rangle
$$

with $h$ selected at random from $R_q$. For a GKP code with

$$
\mathcal{C}=\sqrt{\frac{\lambda}{q}}L,
$$

**Good GKP codes conjecture.** The code is likely to be good, encodes $k=n$ qubits, and has distance

$$
\Delta\geq\min\left\{\sqrt{\frac{n}{\lambda\pi e}},\sqrt{\frac{q}{\lambda}}\right\}.
$$

This conjecture is motivated by numerical evidence for random NTRU lattices and by known lower bounds on their shortest-vector lengths; it predicts that suitable random NTRU-lattice constructions yield good GKP codes.

382203.title: Polynomial-time branchwidth conjecture for graphs embeddable in the torus and projective plane
382203.statement:
Let $H$ be a graph that can be embedded both in the torus and in the projective plane. Consider graphs excluding $H$ as a minor.

**Polynomial-time branchwidth conjecture.** Branchwidth can be computed in polynomial time on $H$-minor-free graphs.

Exact polynomial-time computation of branchwidth is known for graph classes excluding a single-crossing graph as a minor, while the corresponding question for graphs excluding a graph embeddable in both the torus and the projective plane remains open.

382215.title: Polynomial-time homotopy-type conjecture for independence complexes of circle graphs
382215.statement:
Let $G$ be a circle graph, and let $I(G)$ be its independence complex. The size of the input is measured by the number of vertices of $G$. **Polynomial-time homotopy-type conjecture.** The homotopy type of $I(G)$ can be found in polynomial time with respect to the number of vertices of $G$.

This algorithmic conjecture is closely related to Adamaszek's question and would imply polynomial-time determination of the extreme Khovanov spectrum in the relevant setting. The paper establishes polynomial-time computation for independence complexes associated with $4$-braid diagrams, while the general circle-graph problem remains open.
